To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of IGF binding protein 6 is highest in the hindbrain (pontine nuclei), spinal cord (dorsal horn), cranial ganglia (trigeminal and facial ganglia) and dorsal root ganglion.
BP6 is expressed at high levels in the adult brain and sensory ganglia and that its expression is restricted to GABAergic inter neurons in the forebrain.
BP6 is a highly specific marker of GABAergic inter neurons in the adult rat brain and that BP6 mRNA expression is highly restricted in the embryonic nervous system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IGF-II in the nervous system.
identifying the expression of BP6 in the developing and normal adult rat nervous system.
the expression and function of the IGF-II/IGF binding protein 6 complex in the developing and injured nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BP6 mRNA is primarily expressed in sensory ganglia and in the hindbrain where it is likely involved in the modulation of the IGF-II/IGF-I receptor system.
the expression of BP6 in the nervous system is restricted to those structures that have the greatest requirement for the maintenance of sensorimotor integration.
BP6 expression in the CNS is associated with the coordination and maintenance of sensorimotor functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BP6 is primarily expressed in the hindbrain/spinal cord and in sensory ganglia and is associated with the coordination and integration of sensory input from the periphery to the CNS.
IGF-II is expressed in the adult nervous system and that the BP6 protein is the primary IGF-II binding protein in the brain and spinal cord.
the expression profile of BP6 in the nervous system is unique and is associated with the coordination and maintenance of sensorimotor systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BP6 is not a ubiquitous IGF binding protein, but rather a highly restricted protein that is expressed in specific nuclei in the brain, cranial ganglion, and dorsal root neurons.
BP6 mRNA is expressed in a highly restricted pattern in the embryonic and adult nervous system, with the highest expression in the trigeminal ganglion.
IGF-II is the predominant IGF in the CNS and that BP6 is a key regulator of its activity.
